Chapter 10: Returning Changed
The last days of any journey can feel quietly profound, can’t they? You find yourself packing up, saying heartfelt goodbyes to the people who’ve welcomed you in, and there’s this bittersweet mix—sadness at leaving, but also deep gratitude. It’s like you know you’ve shared something important, even if words can’t quite capture it all.
On that final morning, our traveler walks alone through the bush, retracing familiar paths—places that once seemed so foreign, but now feel surprisingly close to home. Every little detail stands out: the curve of a rock, a bird’s distant call, the way sunlight skips across the ground. Each of these moments is tied to a memory—a story told, a song quietly learned.
There’s a moment when he just stops, closes his eyes, and lets the sounds and scents of the land completely surround him. And in that stillness, something shifts. He feels like he truly belongs, connected in a way that goes beyond anything words could explain. It’s clear now: this journey hasn’t just changed what he knows—it’s changed how he sees the world, how he listens, how he moves within it.
He can’t help but think about all the people he’s met along the way—the elders who hold the old songs, the younger ones learning to balance tradition with change, the guides and teachers who are always building bridges between worlds. And he realizes something important: the work of listening, honoring, and remembering? It’s never really finished. It’s a lifelong journey, filled with patience, humility, and care.
As he boards the train and looks out over the land one last time, he knows the songlines are still there—running just beneath the surface, weaving together past and present, land and people, memory and hope. And he carries those connections with him now, like a quiet tune in his heart—a gentle reminder that the world is full of meaning, if you just know how to listen.
